# Independent audit: common targets and saturation deficit

Audited `candidate 80791dd8739dad42` in full. **PASS after the source-count correction now incorporated in Section 1.**

The common-target margin makes each outward-smoothed cap dominate the ordinary through-target cap. The projective cone field is legitimate at an exposed vertex of the complete sampled-base hull. If two different sources use the same target fiber but different common points, their projective fields need not agree. Thus the general construction sums one normalized field per **source**, retaining the bound of at most k(P) fields. Merging fields by distinct target is justified only with an additional common-field hypothesis, as in the separate common-symmetry theorem.

The minimal-circuit affine center in Section 2 is exact linear algebra. The unique dependence is precisely the orthogonal complement of the normal-evaluation range. The resulting affine map need not lie in any target fiber; that missing inclusion is stated explicitly.

For Section 3, a generic base direction has a positive minimum absolute gap on the finite set of other bases. A sufficiently large finite multiple dominates the bounded continuous margins and the finite buffer/width on every other compact fiber, while leaving the own cap unchanged. There are finitely many sign cells, so the saturation baseline is attained. Subtraction from the actual active cap mass gives the nonnegative deficit exactly. At zero deficit, replacing the base tilt preserves the cap mass and continuous normal, hence actual activity and quantile balance. Response weights must be recomputed from the new positive coareas, as the note requires.

If the saturation baseline is positive, a maximizing exposed base can be chosen on its positive side, and its whole fiber is captured by every retargeted cap. If it is zero, the source itself is exposed in the complete base hull. Both claims include arbitrary nonsymmetric fiber shapes. The finite saturating multiple can depend on the cap; a finite balanced menu allows one common sufficiently large choice if desired.

Finally, the active representative compactness is the previously established finite-width clipping compactness. The deficit depends continuously only on the normalized continuous direction through its own-cap mass. Probability-menu compactness and closed continuous balance therefore give attainment of the minimum mean deficit. Since the deficit is nonnegative, a zero minimum is equivalent to a menu supported on its zero set. No positive lower bound on outside coarea follows in general, and no Hessian kernel is promoted to an exact active family.

The note supplies sufficient paying cases and an attained remaining invariant. It does not establish the payment for positive deficit.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
